title: Sit-Stand Desks Improve Productivity, Study Finds
paragraphs: When you think about a hardworking office, you might picture people sitting at desks for hours at a time. But getting up off those chairs could be the key to getting more done!
Research has found that desks that let workers choose between sitting and standing are linked with higher levels of productivity.
A study published in Theoretical and Applied Ergonomics looked at a year's worth of data from 10,000 office workers at a large US company.

The workers had either a normal desk that they just sat at, or one with an adjustable height that let them choose between sitting or standing when they liked. To be part of the study, they had to have been using their desk for one year before it started, and could not change it during the research.

The researchers looked at data from software that tracked the participants' computer use. They found that across the year, workers who used sit-stand desks used their computers an average of 43 minutes more each day compared to people who could only sit to work.
The researchers say this increased productivity could be worth almost an extra $9,000 per employee per year.
That extra activity was far more than just moving a mouse around too. Workers at sit-stand desks generally typed more words and made more keystrokes, suggesting they were doing meaningful work.

Sit-stand desks may have important health benefits too. Instead of having to spend too much time sitting or standing during the day, both of which can cause back and joint pain, sit-stand desks let workers change their position as they feel they need to.
